entities.name: PMID:25427271
observations: Case-control pilot study of 30 systemically healthy urban Indian men: 15 with generalized severe chronic periodontitis and 15 with clinically healthy periodontium.
Periodontitis participants had significantly lower hemoglobin, RBC count, packed-cell volume/hematocrit, and MCHC, and significantly higher MCV and ESR than controls.
ANCOVA using age as covariate found significant between-group hematologic differences; exact P-values and effect estimates were not available in the abstract.

The authors concluded that severe periodontal disease can be linked with anemic status. The abstract did not report serum iron, ferritin, transferrin, TIBC, or transferrin saturation, so biochemical confirmation of anemia of chronic disease was unavailable.

entities.name: Generalized severe chronic periodontitis
observations: The study investigated generalized severe chronic periodontitis in urban Indian males.

entities.name: Anemia of chronic disease
observations: The study title and interpretation link severe chronic periodontitis with anemia of chronic disease, but the accessible abstract reports hematologic changes without direct iron-study confirmation.
